name: Hydra analyze verdicts
description: Aggregate a cycle's review verdicts off the issue's labels, and resolve the CONTRADICTORY state a reviewer-dispatch race can leave behind: both pass and fail present at once. Fail takes precedence, the stale pass label is removed, and the cycle is tagged so the self-learning layer can count how often the race happens. This is the port of orchestrate.sh's `_analyze_verdicts` — see openspec/changes/hydra-flows-first-port ORCHESTRATE-AUDIT.md. Every write is brokered: the credential never reaches this app.
$comment: WHAT WAS WRONG (REVALIDATION-2026-08-02 D1). Three faults, each fatal on its own:
1. `code-contradiction` / `security-contradiction` were `openregister.route`
steps configured with `routes[].when` / `routes[].to`. RouterNode reads
`config.rules[].condition` / `.output` and NOTHING else, so `rulesOf()`
returned [] and every item fell to a `default` that named an EDGE id
rather than an output place — so every item was dropped.
2. `derive`, `skip-code-drop` and `settle` used `config.fields`.
SetFieldsNode reads `set` / `compute` / `rename` / `remove` /
`keepOnlySet`. The steps reported `completed` and set nothing.
3. `drop-security-pass` and `settle` were both `verdict → verdict`
self-loops. The place never empties, so the transitions stay enabled
forever: the run died on `Flow did not settle within 1000 transitions`
with `drop-security-pass` fired 995 times and `settle` never once.
🔑 WHY THIS GRAPH USES EDGE CONDITIONS AND NOT `openregister.route`.
A router is a PER-ITEM split: `FlowEngine::advanceItems()` marks EVERY place
on the firing transition's `to` list and then hands each place only the items
tagged for it. So after a route both branch places hold a token and one of
them holds zero items. That is exactly right when the branches END
separately — which is what hydra-sequencer, hydra-dispatch and
hydra-commit-by-api all do.
It is WRONG when the branches must REJOIN, which is this flow's shape: the
contradiction is resolved and then the verdict is still computed for every
run. `advanceItems()` ASSIGNS to the output place
(`$placeItems[$to] = itemsForOutput(...)`) rather than appending, so whichever
of the two rejoining transitions fires second OVERWRITES the other's items —
and the empty branch is just as likely to be second. Measured on this
instance: a router split rejoining on one place left the join place holding
0 items and `settle` computed nothing.
`FlowEngine::selectTransition()` is the XOR the rejoin needs. Among the
transitions enabled on one place it fires the first whose EDGE-level
`condition` holds, and an edge with no condition is the else. Exactly one
fires, exactly one token moves, and the item survives the rejoin intact.
⚠️ THE EXPRESSION SCOPE WAS ALSO WRONG, and this is invisible in a unit test
of the JsonLogic alone. `FlowExpression::dataFor()` nests the item's record
under `json`, so `{"var": "labels"}` resolves to null — the rules were
verified against a bare record and stored against a flow document. Every
path here is `json.…`, and the label list is `json.labels.body` because
`openconnector.source-call` writes `{status, headers, body, …}` under its
`output` key.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: the rules themselves. Both label dialects are
still checked (`code-review:pass` AND `code-review-pass`) because the colon
form replaced the hyphen form and old issues still carry the old spelling; a
contradiction still resolves to FAIL with the stale pass label deleted at the
forge; and `allPassed` still requires BOTH reviews to have spoken, so one
pass and one silence is not a pass.

$bindings.read-labels.source: The uuid of the Source seeded from flows/hydra-forge.source.json on the target instance. Instance-specific; an importer resolves it by name.

config.$why: The verdict is read from the FORGE rather than from anything this run remembers. A cycle's two reviewers dispatch independently, so the only place their combined state exists is the issue itself.

BOTH label dialects are checked — `code-review:pass` and `code-review-pass`. The shell carried both because the colon form replaced the hyphen form and old issues still hold the old spelling; a port that checked only one would read a real verdict as 'none' and stall the cycle rather than fail loudly. These are DERIVED values, so they are `compute` (JsonLogic) and not `set` (templates): a template substitutes and cannot evaluate.

A contradiction is a RACE, not a verdict: two reviewer dispatches landed an issue in an impossible state. It is resolved rather than reported, because a cycle that stops on it would need a human for something the rule already decides — fail wins. 404 is accepted: the stale label may already be gone, and resolving a contradiction must be idempotent rather than fatal. Only the colon form is deleted — the hyphen form is legacy and the transition flow no longer writes it.

The else of `drop-code-pass` — it carries no `condition`, so `FlowEngine::selectTransition()` only takes it when the contradiction test did not hold. The no-contradiction branch still has to REACH the security check, so it sets the same output key to null and passes through. Without it the common case would dead-end and the flow would complete having decided nothing.
Same race, the other reviewer. Kept as its own pair of edges rather than folded into the first, because the two verdicts are independent and a contradiction in one says nothing about the other.
The else of `drop-security-pass`, for the same reason `skip-code-drop` exists.

verdictCount is how many of the TWO reviews have spoken at all, and allPassed requires both — a cycle with one pass and one silence is not a pass. The shell computed exactly this and the distinction is load-bearing: treating a missing verdict as a pass is the green-but-dead shape this whole change exists to remove. A contradiction has already been resolved to fail above, so it is counted as a verdict here.
